ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $OB$ is the bisector of $\angle AOC$, $\angle COD = \frac{1}{3}\angle BOD$, $\angle COD = 17^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle AOD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ $\angle COD = \frac{1}{3} \angle BOD$, and $\angle COD = 17^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BOC = 2\angle COD = 2 \times 17^\circ = 34^\circ$,\\
since OB is the bisector of $\angle AOC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AOC = 2\angle BOC = 2 \times 34^\circ = 68^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AOD = \angle AOC + \angle COD = 68^\circ + 17^\circ = \boxed{85^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, four rays share vertex O; ray OA is the lowest ray, close to horizontal and pointing to the right, OB is above OA, OC is above OB, and OD is the highest, left-leaning ray. Therefore, from OA to OD, one passes through OB and OC in sequence, and ∠AOD is composed by adding the adjacent ∠AOB, ∠BOC, and ∠COD; ∠BOD is composed by adding ∠BOC and ∠COD. Reasoning: It is known that OB is the angle bisector of ∠AOC, so ∠AOB = ∠BOC. It is also known that ∠COD = 17°, and ∠COD = 1/3 ∠BOD, so ∠BOD = 3 × 17° = 51°. Because ∠BOD = ∠BOC + ∠COD, ∠BOC = 51° - 17° = 34°. Thus ∠AOB = 34°. Finally, ∠AOD = ∠AOB + ∠BOC + ∠COD = 34° + 34° + 17° = 85°.
